the center of mass position distribution of a quantum oscillator with many degrees of freedoms can be considered Gaussian, if the energy of the oscillator is fixed and the initial wave function is a product of excited states or even and odd superposition of coherent states.

the center of mass of a quantum particle can be treated as a classical particle if its energy is large enough, and that the central limit theorem can be applied to obtain a classical description for the center of masses of a large number of particles.

the central limit theorem allows one to obtain a classical distribution for the center of the mass tomogram in the limit \hbar \rightarrow 0$ if the initial distribution of the quantum system is Gaussian.

the center of mass distribution of a system with $N$ degrees of freedom in the limit of $N \to \infty and \hbar \rightarrow 0$ tends to a $\delta$-function.

the classical limit for the distribution of the center of the mass of the system is a delta function.

the center of mass distribution is not a quantum mechanical observable, but it is a classical observable.
